Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The present petition has been filed U/s 166 & 140 M.V.Act seeking compensation of Rs.
40,00,000/- alongwith interest from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization on account of injuries suffered by petitioner Arif (aged 21 years) in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 24.01.2017.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 24.01.2017 at about 8:15 PM, petitioner Arif alongwith his friends Altmas and Naim were going to their home from the work place on the petitioner's motorcycle bearing registration no.
DL-11ST-2583 which was being driven by petitioner and when they reached at Narela Bawana Road,
J.J. Colony, Bawana, Delhi, suddenly offending vehicle i.e. TATA ACE bearing No. DL-1LS-6830 driven by respondent no. 1 came at a very high speed from wrong direction and hit the petitioner's vehicle due to which the petitioner sustained multiple grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Maharishi Valmiki Hospital, Pooth Khurd, Delhi, where he was medically examined.

A case U/s 279/338 IPC and u/s 146/196, 3/181 M.V. Act was registered at PS. Narela, vide FIR No. 72/17 with regard MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 to the accident in question.

The petitioner has claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver-cum- owner and was duly insured with respondent no. 2/Liberty Videocon General Insurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.

sentences.text: 3. In his written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. driver-cum- owner stated that petitioner met with the accident due to his own negligence as he was driving the vehicle in zig-zag manner and when the vehicle of respondent No. 1 came in front of them, then in order to save themselves they collided with the offending vehicle.

It is also stated that the driver of the TATA ACE bearing No.
DL-1LS-6830 was having valid license and therefore, the present petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has been claimed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 2/insurance company and thus, insurance company is liable to pay compensation, if any to the petitioner.
4. Respondent no. 2/insurance company had filed its reply stating that the driver of the offending vehicle was not found having commercial driving license.

It is further stated that the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation as the cover note was reported to be misplaced and no premium was received against alleged covernote qua the offending vehicle.

On the other hand, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver cum owner and insurance company have not examined any witness and their evidence was closed vide order dated 25.09.2024.
7. This Tribunal has carefully perused DAR/claim petition, evidence led by parties has been duly appreciated.
All documents and material relied upon & proved considered.
Arguments addressed by respective counsels considered.
Legal position, both statutory and binding MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 applicable precedents, has been appreciated.

10. PW1/Injured was not cross-examined on behalf of driver cum owner.
However, he was cross
- examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company.
During the same, he stated that there were three persons on the motorcycle and he himself was driving the motorccyle on the day of accident.
He further stated that the offending vehicle came from the front and took a right turn and took his motorcycle whereas he was going straight away.
He MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 further stated that he and Altmas were wearing helmet at the time of accident.
He further stated that he was conscious after the accident and himself noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle.
He admitted that he has not filed any document to show expenses of Rs.55,000/- on transportation.

11. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross- examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
Moreover, FIR No. 72/2017 (which is part of DAR) is shown to have been registered on the date of accident on the statement of petitioner himself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant/petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

12. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at Maharishi Valmiki Hospital, shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 24.01.2017 at 8:50 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.
13. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the criminal case, have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely Mohd. Mansoor has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s. 279/338 IPC 146/196, 3/181 M.V. Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent Aarif vs Md. Mansoor on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59497742/
4 driving of offending vehicle.

14. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver cum owner of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.
Reliance placed on Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Kamlesh & Ors, MAC APP. No. 530/2008 passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court on 11.11.2008.

Further, it is worth mentioning that the insurance company had settled the claims vide order dated 31.07.2018 towards the other two injured in the present accident in MACP No. 411/17 and 412/17 without recovery rights meaning thereby that the accident or the liability of the insurance company to pay compensation is not disputed.

16. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he has sustained grievous injuries in the Motor Vehicular Accident which has occurred on 24.01.2017 at about 8:15 pm at Narela Bawana Road, J.J. Colony, Bawana, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. TATA ACE bearing No. DL-1LS-6830 by respondent no. 1.

Thus,
issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

17. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
18.

It has been duly established that petitioner sustained injuries as per his MLC in the road accident which took place on 24.01.2017 at about MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 8:15 pm at Narela Bawana Road, J.J. Colony, Bawana, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. TATA ACE bearing No. DL-1LS-6830 by respondent no. 1.
19.

The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Honble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:

"16. "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of Aarif vs Md. Mansoor on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59497742/
5 the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same, consistency and uniformity,
and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."

20. These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
"10. The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

11. The general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".

22. Accordingly, the entitlement of petitioner to just compensation is being assessed in the background of well settled parameters and guidelines as discussed herein-above.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 23.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was taken to Maharishi MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD: 11.12.2024 Valmiki Hospital, Delhi, where he was medically examined and thereafter, he was treated in Lok Nayak Hospital and discharged on 31.01.2017.
Further, he was treated at Bharat Nursing Home and Trauma Center from 27.06.2017 and discharged on 08.07.2017 though his medical treatment continued even during the course of his testimony.

24. It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills (which are part of Ex. PW1/4 colly) to the tune of Rs. 1,03,253/-.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 1,03,253/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
LOSS OF INCOME 25.
PW1 has deposed that he was 27 years of age and was working as car mechanic prior to the accident and was earning Rs. 15,000/- per month.
He further deposed that due to grievous injuries he suffered economic loss.

Counsel for insurance company, he deposed that he had no document to show that he was earning Rs. 15,000/- per month at the time of accident.

26. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for injured argued that due to the injuries suffered by him, he could not work for considerable period and thus, he has suffered loss of income and as such, appropriate compensation be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

27. The treatment record i.e., Discharge Summary of Lok Nayak Hospital (which is part of Ex.
PW1/4 colly), of petitioner shows that he had suffered lacerated wound over right knee exposing Aarif vs Md. Mansoor on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59497742/

He also relied upon the treatment record of Bharat Nursing Home and Trauma Center dated 08.07.2017, 17.07.2017, 26.07.2017, 04.08.2017, 15.08.2017, 20.09.2017, 23.10.2017,

In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess in assessing the loss of income.

It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD:
11.12.2024 sustained multiple fractures as mentioned in his treatment record due to the accident.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at least for a period of 18 months or so including his recovery period.

28. During the course of arguments, Ld. counsel for petitioner fairly conceded that for want of any cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioner regarding his monthly income, his income may be considered as per Minimum Wages Act applicable in the State of Delhi in order to calculate the loss of income.
He vehemently argued that petitioner was working as a car mechanic at the time of accident and thus, minimum wages of a skilled person be considered in order to calculate loss of income.
29. It may be noted here that no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove monthly income of injured/petitioner at the time of accident in question.
The petitioner has also failed to file his educational qualification documents or to show that he was a skilled person working as car mechanic.
No evidence has been brought by the petitioner that he was doing the work of car mechanic at the time of accident.
Accordingly, he is considered as "unskilled".
The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs. 9,724/- per month as on the date of accident which is 24.01.2017.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 1,75,032/- (Rs. 9,724/- x 18) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

"15.

sentences.text: It is settled law that a particular amount cannot be fixed on pain and sufferings for all cases as is varies from case to case.
Judicial notice can be taken on the fact that since the petitioner had got injuries/fracture as aforesaid, he mighthave suffered acute pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries.
He might have also consumed heavy dose of anti-biotic etc. and also might have remained without movements of his body for a considerable period of time.

In order to ascertain the pain and sufferings compensation, I am guided by the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No.709/02, date of decision:

31.

As already considered, the petitioner required treatment for a considerable period from the date of accident and remained incapacitated to MACP No. 407/17; FIR No. 72/17; PS. Narela DOD:
11.12.2024 resume his work of earnings for at least a period of 18 months owing to grievous injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 71% in relation to his right lower limb.
The petitioner was having a short limb of right lower limb which is of 1 inch shorter than the left limb.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings, inconvenience and mental trauma on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 1,50,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain & sufferings.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 32.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 71% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him and his continued treatment for considerable period and the permanent disability suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
